visual_argument: Reasoning is a stair and every score is its rise at one scale, 0.06 m per point: the junk dose shortens the climb landing by landing, the skipped thinking is a stringer with its treads gone, and the repair rebuilds a stair that still stops under the brass line where the base model stood.
build_risk: Frame 3 is five landings on stone piers joined by short limestone flights, descending from 72.1 to 57.2 at one scale under a brass datum at 77.2, seen through a long lens from a low oblique. It has to read as built stone with nosings, stringers, piers and cast shadows at 432 px and never as a step chart or a bar chart in hardware, which is what the judges charged no. 53's benchmark frames with. Built from the chassis stair_flight, landing_pier and datum_wall models in txthree under the lastLight key.
distinct_from_recent: No. 56 (Oct 21) was a machine shop of machined parts and taped bays in interiors and plan reliefs under a comal lit accent. No. 55 (Oct 20) was floodlit operating rooms and walls of steel container ends. No. 54 (Oct 18) was lastLight brush country with windmills, cattle and counted boxes. This deck is one built thing, a freestanding limestone and weathering steel stair in an empty dark field, measured vertically against one brass line, with no interior, no counted isotype and no plan relief except one native scale surface on frame 2.
